To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the C-type cyclin is a dual function regulator.
cyclin C is an essential regulator of stress-responsive gene expression and that it also regulates mitochondrial fission in response to stress.

the stress regulated transcriptional repressor cyclin C translocates from nucleus to cytoplasm where, independent of its cyclin-dependent kinase (Cdk) partner, it mediates mitochondrial fission and programmed cell death (Pcd) by interacting with mitochondrial fission machinery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of cyclin-dependent kinases in regulating the expression of stress-responsive genes.
understanding how cells coordinate gene expression and cell death pathways to effect an appropriate response to environmental stress.
understanding the role of cyclin-dependent kinase 8 in regulating the stress response.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cyclin C-Crk1-Cdc4-Cdk8 complex plays a central and critical role in regulating the stress response in budding yeast by coordinating transcription and mitochondrial dynamics.
the cyclin C-CdK8 complex regulates stress responsive gene expression by repressing transcription.
cyclin C is a master coordinator of stress response gene expression that is essential for the execution of mitochondrial fission and apoptosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cyclin C is a master regulator of the stress response that controls gene expression, mitochondrial dynamics, and PCD.

the stress regulated destruction of cyclin C is necessary to relieve the repression of stress responsive genes, which in turn, promotes the expression of genes that are important for mitochondrial fission and the induction of PCD.

the conserved cyclin C-Cyclin dependent kinase (CdK) complex plays a central role in the regulation of stress-responsive transcription and that the cyclin C-CdK8 subunit of the complex is released from the transcription machinery and translocates to the cytoplams where it regulates mitochondrial fission and programmed cell death.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cyclin C is a key player in the cell's stress response.
the stress response is a tightly regulated process that is orchestrated by a conserved cyclin.
a transcription factor can play dual roles in stress response by coupling changes in transcription to organelle function and cell survival.
